item.title: Improving protection for motorcycle police officers
item.description: Motorcycle protective clothing certified to the highest protection standard under the EN 17092 series is primarily designed with recreational riders in mind. However, whether this standard adequately addresses the elevated occupational hazards faced by professional riders, such as police officers, is a growing concern. Unlike leisure riders, motorcycle police officers operate routinely in high-risk environments, responding to emergencies, conducting escorts, and patrolling in all weather conditions. Under the Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) Regulation, equipment must be suitable for the specific operational risks of the user. item.title: New European standard for learning towers adopted
item.description: ANEC welcomed the adoption of a new European Standard for learning towers, also known as ‘kitchen helpers’. EN 18122 ‘High chairs and learning towers – Learning towers – Requirements and test methods’ was developed by CEN/TC 364 ‘High chairs and learning towers’, following a proposal from ANEC. ANEC raised the issue in 2021, as their analysis suggested that the products themselves not only presented fall and entrapment (and possibly other) hazards, but could also give rise to hazards by providing access to dangers such as thermal injuries, lacerations and poisonings when used close to kitchen work surfaces and in bathrooms. item.title: Join an Academic Standards Day near you!
item.description: This autumn, EDU4Standards is bringing its Academic Standards Days to Ireland (15 October), Sweden (16 October), Belgium (26 October), Norway (18 November) and Finland (3 December). Designed for students, researchers, educators, and standards professionals, this series aims to increase interest and deepen the understanding of standardization within academia, laying the foundations to train a new generation of experts. Through presentations, panel discussions and workshops, participants will gain practical insights into standardization and connect with experts from academia, industry and the standards community. item.title: Advancing European standards and regulations for 3D bioprinting
item.description: Following the Putting Science into Standards (PSIS) workshop that took place in October 2025 on the topic of 3D bioprinting, a scientific article was published in the Trends in Biotechnology Journal, together with the European Commission’s Joint Research Centre (JRC) and Directorate-General for Research and Innovation (RTD). Please find it here for your information. Background about the PSIS initiative Putting-Science-Into-Standards (PSIS) is a joint initiative developed by CEN, CENELEC and the Joint Research Centre (JRC) of the European Commission. Its aim is to facilitate the identification of emerging science and technology areas that could benefit from standardization to enable innovation and promote industrial competitiveness. item.title: WE NORM THE FUTURE | Summit 2026: Standards for Europe’s future
item.description: Following the strong response to its inaugural edition in 2025, the WE NORM THE FUTURE | Summit returns this autumn. Austrian Standards will host a series of Expert Talks addressing key issues for Europe’s standardization community. Most of the Expert Talks will be held in German. Live audio translation and subtitles in English, French and Italian will be available throughout via the streaming page, making the discussions accessible to an international audience. The series opens on 8 October with the Expert Talks on the EU Standardization Strategy. Under the title “Resilient. Democratic. Competitive. item.title: Hydrogen on track: new standards support fuel-cell-powered rolling stock
item.description: As Europe continues its transition towards cleaner and more sustainable mobility, hydrogen is emerging as one of the technologies that could help reduce the environmental impact of rail transport, particularly on lines where conventional electrification is difficult or economically challenging. The EN IEC 63341 series on hydrogen and fuel cell systems for rolling stock provides an important standardization framework to support this development. Within Europe, this work is addressed by CENELEC/TC 9X ‘Electrical and electronic applications for railways’, building on international standardization carried out within IEC/TC 9 ‘Electrical equipment and systems for railways’, in cooperation with IEC/TC 105 ‘Fuel cell technologies’. item.title: CEN and CENELEC contribute to Europe-Africa dialogue on greener ICT value chains
item.description: On 24 September 2026, CEN and CENELEC participated in the ECOS and InDiCo-Global workshop "Towards a Greener ICT Value Chain: Standards, Policies and Best Practices Dialogue for Europe and Africa" in Nairobi, Kenya. Bringing together policymakers, standards bodies, environmental organizations, industry representatives and civil society stakeholders, the event provided a platform for exchange on standards and policies supporting greener and more circular ICT value chains. During the session on sharing best practices in standardization, the three European Standardization Organizations (ESOs) presented the European experience in fostering inclusive participation in standardization.
